scientific_limitations_and_integrity: Exact coupling relies on rotational invariance and the one-deleted-edge property of a simple cycle. Biased vertex orientations differ from the standard uniform-neighbor one-out law except at \(p=1/2\). The CLT requires fixed p in (0,1); the Poisson law requires \(np_n\) to have a finite limit at an orientation endpoint. Circular run counts were known previously and are not asserted to be independently new. Mathematical proof and finite checks have been conducted, but independent external validation and exhaustive priority verification have not.
title: Optimal spanning-tree/one-out coupling on a cycle: exact law and Poisson–Gaussian regimes
